question.text: If the 10-year G-Sec yield is 6.5% and average inflation is 2%, what is the real interest rate?

explanation.text: The Logic: Real interest rate = Nominal interest rate - Inflation rate = 6.5% - 2% = 4.5%. Page 32 of the workbook uses this exact example of a 10-year G-Sec yield of 6.5 per cent and average inflation of 2 per cent producing a 4.5 per cent real interest rate. The Trap: Adding the rates (6.5% + 2%) gives the wrong answer. The real rate is always nominal minus inflation. Note: Per page 33, when RBI hikes rates and real rates rise, FPI debt flows tend to increase, raising dollar supply and supporting INR strength.
